purpose: Assesses whether the organization can prevent or detect an adversary stealing account names and passwords or other credentials associated with AI systems and agent configurations.
summary: Credential Access consists of techniques for stealing credentials like account names and passwords. Techniques used to get credentials include keylogging or credential dumping, as well as harvesting credentials embedded in AI agent configuration files. Using legitimate credentials can give adversaries access to systems, make them harder to detect, and provide the opportunity to create more accounts to help achieve their goals.
expectedStatementElements: How credentials embedded in AI agent configuration files (API keys, tokens, connection strings) are protected from exposure
What secrets management practices are used for AI pipeline and inference service credentials
How the organization detects credential dumping or keylogging attempts on systems with access to AI resources
Whether AI agent and MCP server configuration files are scanned for hardcoded secrets before deployment
evidenceExamples: Secrets management/vault configuration for AI pipeline and inference service credentials
Scanning tool results (e.g., secret scanners) run against AI agent and MCP configuration files
Credential rotation policy and records for AI system service accounts and API keys
Endpoint detection/monitoring for credential dumping or keylogging activity on AI-adjacent systems
commonGaps: API keys and tokens are hardcoded directly in AI agent or MCP configuration files rather than a secrets vault
No scanning process catches hardcoded secrets in agent configuration before deployment
Credentials for AI service accounts are rarely or never rotated
interviewQuestions: Are our AI agent's API keys and tokens stored in a secrets vault, or hardcoded in config files?
Do we scan agent or MCP configuration files for hardcoded secrets before they go live?
How often do we rotate credentials used by our AI pipelines and inference services?
Would we detect an attempt to dump credentials from a system that has access to our AI resources?
